title: Resolve billing ghost counts from ephemeral namespace fallbacks
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Summary: Intermittent 'ghost' billing counts have been observed where usage attributed to ephemeral namespaces (created by fallback proxies and temporary token swaps) is not being reconciled to the parent project/org. Symptoms surface during rolling upgrades of gateway proxies and during transient KV-cache misses: requests are accepted by a fallback path that stamps an ephemeral namespace id; downstream metering aggregates the ephemeral id separately, producing duplicate or orphaned billing rows.

Observed behavior:
- Spike pattern: small, short-lived billing spikes (~1-3% of overall traffic) correlated with gateway rolling restarts and with deployments of the rate-limiter service.
- Metering logs show entries with namespace_id like "ephemeral-<hex>" that never map to a known project id in the tenant-mapping service.
- Aggregation pipeline emits separate billing windows for those ephemeral ids; final billing normalization does not re-attribute them because the ephemeral id TTL expired before reconciliation runs.
- Affected customers see short over-billing in daily reports and then a corrective adjustment 24–48h later; some customers reported unexpected invoice line items.

Reproduction (dev):
1) Start local gateway cluster with failover proxy enabled and enable ephemeral-namespace fallback flag.
2) Trigger a rolling restart of the gateway while concurrently executing high QPS multi-tenant workloads (simulated using load-generator).
3) Observe metrics: metering.ingress.unattributed_count increments; billing pipeline creates separate windows for ephemeral ids.

Root cause hypothesis: The fallback proxy path creates ephemeral namespace IDs when tenant resolution fails (race on cache refresh during upgrades). These ephemeral IDs are short-lived and are not inserted into the canonical tenant-store. The metering pipeline treats namespace_id as primary key for aggregation and lacks a reconciliation step that maps ephemeral ids back to parent claims when the tenant-store learns the mapping post-fact.

Immediate impact: Incorrect short-term billing attribution and potential invoice confusion for customers during infra churn. Also causes alert churn in billing-monitoring dashboards.

Work items (high level):
- Instrumentation: add tracing tags on requests that take fallback path and emit 'ephemeral_origin' flag into metering events.
- Normalization: add a normalization stage in the streaming aggregator that attempts to resolve ephemeral namespace IDs against the tenant-store with a 48h backfill window; if resolved, re-emit corrected aggregation rows and mark originals as reconciled.
- Atomicity: ensure token handoff logic performs an atomic claim transfer when proxy swaps token ownership to avoid transient un-resolvable claims.
- Alerts: new alert 'billing.ghost_rate > 0.1%' during rolling upgrades.
- Tests: unit tests for normalization logic, integration test simulating rolling restart, and end-to-end billing correctness test in staging with synthetic tenants.

Rollout plan: implement normalization and instrumentation behind feature flag 'normalize_ephemeral_namespaces'. Run in staging for two full rolling-upgrade cycles. If stable, enable in canary region for 48h and monitor invoice diffs and ghost-rate. Then full rollout in release meter-2026.03.

Risk/mitigation: re-attributing billing rows after settlement could affect invoicing; plan to only perform reconciliation for events within a 48h window and surface reconciliation adjustments via an audit log and customer notices if remediations cross billing cutoff thresholds.

proposed_fixes: 1) Add 'ephemeral_origin' boolean and 'parent_claim_hint' optional field to metering events emitted by gateway/fallback proxies.

2) Implement normalization stage in streaming-aggregator: for ephemeral ids, call tenant-store with exponential backoff up to 48h; if mapping appears, re-attribute aggregated rows and emit reconciliation event.
3) Make token-handoff in gateway atomic: swap claim pointer and write a transaction in tenant-store before evicting old claim from cache.
4) Add E2E scenario in staging that runs rolling restart while validating no new ghost rows are created with feature flag enabled.
5) Add dashboard and PagerDuty rule: billing.ghost_rate > 0.5% for 5m triggers page.
acceptance_criteria: Normalization stage backfills and re-attributes ephemeral namespace events within 48h in staging runs.
No customer-visible duplicate billing rows produced during controlled rolling restart test (staging).
New instrumentation surfaces ephemeral-origin rate in billing dashboards and test alerts fire appropriately.
Code reviewed, security sign-off obtained, and feature flag controls rollout.
Performance: aggregator end-to-end latency increase <5% when normalization flag enabled under normal traffic.
